Bug_Title: EC: Call to equals() comparing different types (EC_UNRELATED_TYPES)
Bug_Details:
This method calls equals(Object) on two references of different
class types and analysis suggests they will be to objects of different classes
at runtime. Further, examination of the equals methods that would be invoked suggest that either
this call will always return false, or else the equals method is not symmetric (which is
a property required by the contract
for equals in class Object).
Bug_Explanation: The bug is present in the showBug() method where an object of ClassA is compared with an object of ClassB using the equals() method. Since ClassA's equals() method always returns false, the comparison will always return false, regardless of the actual content of the objects. This violates the symmetry property of the equals() method, leading to incorrect results.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test case `testShowBug` calls the method `BuggyCode.showBug()` which triggers the bug. This is because the `showBug` method compares an object of `ClassA` with an object of `ClassB` using the `equals` method. Since `ClassA's` `equals` method always returns false, this comparison will always return false, regardless of the actual content of the objects. This violates the symmetry property of the `equals` method, leading to incorrect results.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results confirm the presence of the bug. The test code triggers the bug by comparing an object of ClassA with an object of ClassB using the equals() method. Since the objects are of different classes, the equals() method of ClassA is called, which always returns false, violating the symmetry principle of the equals() method. The test assertion expects false as the result, which is the expected behavior, confirming the bug triggering.
